title: Ye Trembling Souls, Dismiss Your Fears
description: Ye Trembling Souls, Dismiss Your Fears in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Benjamin Beddome wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 643 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Fear not”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ye trem-bling souls, dis-miss your fears; Be mer-cy all your theme; For mer-cy like a riv-er flows, In one per-pet-ual stream.

lines: Ye trembling souls, dismiss your fears;
For mercy like a river flows,
Fear not the powers of earth and hell;
His arm will all their rage repel,
Fear not the want of outward good;
Grant them supplies of daily food,
Fear not that he will e'er forsake,

licence: Public domain: Benjamin Beddome died in 1795.
credits: Words by Benjamin Beddome (1717–1795), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
